header:
Date: 2026-03-04 | Time: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 42m
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Lin (Halo Head of ML), Tom Alvarez (CTO), Lena Ortiz (Infra)
summary: Discovery focused on unit economics for Redwood hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Customer is cost-sensitive, target budget ~$20k/month for inference, wants clear levers: batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization, and dedicated pool sizing. Security and data residency briefly confirmed (SOC 2 + SSO), Halo will share prompts and token counts for a baseline. Redwood to propose pricing scenarios and run a quick throughput test against sample workload.
topics: per-token pricing ranges for hosted inference
effect of batching on throughput and unit cost
KV/prefix caching to cut recurrent prefix cost
Dedicated capacity sizing and committed pricing
Private/VPC considerations and security (SOC2, KMS, SSO)
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh I think we have about 40 minutes, we'll focus on cost and unit economics for your inference workloads. quick intros?
[00:10] Maya: Maya here, head of ML at Halo. we've got a couple production agents, about 7 models in rotation, mostly 13B and 34B open weights.
[00:20] Tom: Tom here, CTO, i'll be watching infra and budget.
[00:25] Jordan: great. Samir is our solutions engineer, he'll go into batching and throughput.
[00:30] Samir: hi all. quick q up front, what are your target p95 latency and monthly budget numbers?
[00:37] Maya: p95 latency ideally <150ms for short answer queries (<256 tokens). budget, we were thinking, um around 20k a month to start for the initial rollout.
[00:46] Jordan: ok good. so two levers we'll talk about: hosting vs Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private. Hosted gets you fastest time to value and simple per-token pricing, Dedicated gives predictable unit cost and isolation, Private for regulated workloads.
[00:58] Samir: on per-token pricing, to set expectations, our baseline hosted ranges depend on model and quantization. ballpark numbers: for 13B models on optimized runtime with q4 or q5 quant we typically see 0.5 to 2.0 cents per 1k tokens; for 34B it's more like 1.5 to 6.0 cents per 1k tokens. those are net of common batching gains but without aggressive KV caching.
[01:20] Lena: wait small sanity check: 0.5 cents per 1k tokens? that seems low, can you repeat units?
[01:25] Samir: yeah sorry, 0.5 to 2.0 US cents per 1,000 tokens. so $0.005 to $0.02 per 1k tokens. I know pricing formats vary, we can send the table.
[01:35] Maya: ok that makes more sense. how does batching affect that? we get a lot of short sessions so i worry about tail latency.
[01:43] Samir: great q. batching increases throughput and reduces per-token compute overhead; with continuous batching and dynamic batch sizing we often see 2x-5x effective unit cost improvement for high concurrency scenarios. but it trades off with latency: bigger batches can push p95 up. Redwood's serving runtime supports latency SLOs so you can cap batch size or use small latency-first pools for critical routes.
[02:05] Tom: and caching? we have lots of conversational agents that repeat prefixes.
[02:09] Samir: KV/prefix caching is big for conversation-heavy workloads. if your agents reuse context or system prompts, caching can cut token compute by 30% to 70% depending on reuse patterns. we do automatic prefix caching in hosted and Dedicated, and you can bring your own cache policies in Private.
[02:25] Maya: that could move us under budget if the reuse is high. what's the typical delta between hosted and Dedicated pricing then?
[02:32] Jordan: Dedicated is structured as reserved capacity (GPU pools) plus lower per-token compute because you're not paying the hosted margin. for example a committed pool sized for your throughput might reduce unit cost by ~20-40% vs hosted depending on utilization. exact numbers depend on model, q, and your concurrency.
[02:48] Lena: any quick estimate for our 34B models at 100 qps average with 200 token responses?
[02:54] Samir: rough calc: 100 qps * 200 tokens * 60s * 30 days = 36M tokens/month. at 3 cents per 1k tokens that's about $1,080/month; at 1.5 cents it's $540/month. those per-1k figures were examples; if you target Dedicated and better batching we could push effective per-1k down to 0.8-1.2 cents which would make big diff. I'm simplifying a bit — we'll run an exact baseline on your prompt set.
[03:20] Tom: math check—36M tokens, yep that aligns. but i think our agents have bursts to 400 qps, so need headroom.
[03:27] Samir: capacity planning note: Dedicated pools can autoscale and you can provision burst capacity, or we can do hybrid routing — hosted fallback for spikes. that hedges cost vs safety.
[03:38] Maya: on the security front we need SOC2, SSO (SAML), KMS key control. can hosted meet that?
[03:45] Jordan: Redwood hosted is SOC 2 compliant, supports SSO/SAML, and we offer customer-managed KMS in Private and Dedicated (for VPC private deployments). for hosted we offer encryption at rest and in transit and detailed audit logs; if you need HSM-backed key custody that's part of Private.
[04:01] Lena: and data residency? we need EU-only for a few models.
[04:05] Jordan: yes we have region routing and can pin workloads to EU-only data centers for Dedicated and Private; hosted can be regionally routed too but if strict contractual residency is required we usually recommend Dedicated or Private.
[04:16] Maya: any gotchas on quantization quality? our evaluation cares about subtle safety/answer drift.
[04:22] Samir: good point. lower-bit quant (q4/q5) usually preserves quality well for many open models, but we always run evals on your prompts. Redwood Optimize recommends quant levels per workload and flags quality regression. if you need zero-regression we run canary rollouts with A/B evaluation.
[04:38] Tom: ok so next steps, we want a concrete cost model: hosted per-token table, Dedicated committed pricing with GPU sizing, and an initial benchmark using our prompts for burst+steady state.
[04:49] Jordan: yep. i'll send the pricing sheet and batching/caching whitepaper. Samir will run the bench, but we need your prompt set and sample traffic shape.
[04:57] Maya: i'll drop a csv with ~200 sample sessions and token counts by tomorrow.
[05:02] Jordan: perfect. can we tentatively schedule a 45m follow-up next week to review the baseline?
[05:06] Tom: yes week of 3/9 works.
[05:09] Jordan: great thanks all. we'll follow up with the artifacts and a proposed Dedicated config + cost scenarios.
[05:16] Maya: thanks everyone, bye.
[05:18] Jordan: thanks, bye.
